title: Power Automate: debug desktop flows using variable default values
summary: The briefing passes: the maker setting, debugging command, licensing and roadmap details are supported. Its warning about unprotected sensitive input defaults and its distinction between roadmap assertions and documented behaviour are accurate.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: In Power Automate for desktop, the maker setting is Variables pane > flow variable > Edit flow variable > Default value.
claims.quote: The flow designer lets you inspect and control the values of flow variables directly from the Variables pane ... Double-click a flow variable (or use its menu) to open Edit flow variable. ... Default value: The value applied when running the flow with default values.

claims.claim: An API operation for setting a flow variable's debugging default value is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse flow variable default value API desktop flow debug; Power Platform API PowerShell desktop flow variable debugging default values. Opened Manage variables, v2 schema and Desktop Flow Binary reference; no operation or property documents setting this debugging default.

claims.where: controls[1].ui/api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no dedicated tenant or environment UI setting or API switch for variable defaults in debug runs as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate default values tenant debug setting; Power Platform API PowerShell desktop flow debugging defaults disable environment setting. Opened Manage variables, Manage feature settings and List tenant settings; no feature-specific switch found.

claims.claim: Makers can assign a default value to a flow variable in the desktop flow designer.
claims.quote: For each flow variable, you can: ... Define a default value and default data type used when starting a run with defaults.

claims.claim: The Edit flow variable dialog lets a maker set a default data type.
claims.quote: Default data type: The type used for the default value.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Run from here with default values starts execution from a selected action using configured variable defaults.
claims.quote: You can start execution from a specific action and use each variable's default value instead of recomputing it. ... The flow runs from that action using the configured defaults.

claims.claim: Learn describes variable defaults as helping test scenarios without modifying actions.
claims.quote: These capabilities help you test different scenarios without modifying actions or restarting the flow from the beginning.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Default values of sensitive input variables are not protected in action modals.
claims.quote: The default value of an input variable is visible in the creating or editing dialog when sensitivity is enabled. ... The default values aren't protected in the action modals and the flow definition in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Default values of sensitive input variables are not protected in the flow definition in Dataverse.
claims.quote: The default values aren't protected in the action modals and the flow definition in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Variable default values contribute to the desktop flow definition stored in Dataverse using v2 schema.
claims.quote: The limit applies to the definition of the desktop flow saved in Dataverse, which can't exceed 16M characters. The issue can occur with a large desktop flow, such as when actions have large property values or variables have large default values.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Marking a variable as sensitive masks its value in the designer UI.
claims.quote: Mark as sensitive: Masks the variable value in the UI.

claims.claim: Learn describes sensitive-variable masking during debugging as basic protection against third parties looking at the developer's screen.
claims.quote: Masking sensitive variables during debugging provides only a basic form of protection to developers from third parties looking at their screens.

claims.claim: Existing desktop flow sharing governs who can manage and edit a shared flow.
claims.quote: To enable other makers to manage your flow and collaborate on it, share it with them with Co-owner access.

claims.claim: A separate Microsoft Learn walkthrough tells makers to delete default values before leaving desktop flow authoring.
claims.quote: Delete all default values before you leave the desktop flow authoring experience in Power Automate Desktop.

claims.claim: Learn says flows built or edited with Power Automate for desktop 2.14 or later cannot be opened or run in older versions.
claims.quote: Flows built or edited with Power Automate for desktop version 2.14 or above are incompatible with older versions of Power Automate for desktop. You can't use older versions of Power Automate for desktop to open or run these flows.

claims.claim: The Manage variables page lists one known issue.
claims.quote: Known issues and limitations ... Issue: Flows built or edited with Power Automate for desktop version 2.14 or above are incompatible with older versions of Power Automate for desktop. ... Workarounds: None.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no new data access introduced by this variable-default debugging feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate Run from here with default values data access permissions. Opened Manage variables, v2 schema and Secure your data; read desktop-flow security search excerpt. No new feature-specific data access is stated.
